guides.title: Register a company (Pty Ltd) with ASIC
guides.summary: A company is a separate legal entity, so you register it with ASIC to get an Australian Company Number (ACN) before it can trade. Every director must have a director ID before being appointed, and the company pays an annual review fee every year it stays registered.
guides.authority: Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC); director IDs are issued by Australian Business Registry Services (ABRS)
guides.timeframe: About 15 minutes online once you have everything ready; confirmation usually within 2 business days if documents are complete and the fee is paid.
guides.cost_summary: A$636 to register a proprietary company (from 1 July 2026), then a A$342 annual review fee each year. Director IDs are free.
before_you_start: Make sure a company suits you: sole traders, partnerships and trusts do not register with ASIC as companies. A company has extra legal duties and ongoing costs.
Every director must apply for their own director ID before they are appointed. It is free, done through ABRS, and you keep it for life even if you change companies.

To apply for a director ID online you need a Digital ID such as myID with at least Standard identity strength, plus your ATO-held residential address and details from two verification documents (for example a notice of assessment). Giving your TFN is optional but speeds things up.
Choose a name that shows legal status (for example 'Example Pty Ltd') and check it on ASIC's name availability search, or let ASIC use your ACN as the name.
Decide your state or territory of registration, registered office address and principal place of business.
Decide your internal rules: the replaceable rules in the Corporations Act 2001, your own constitution, or a mix.

Work out the share structure and members. For each member you need name and address and written consent; for each director and secretary you need full name (including former names), home address, date and place of birth, and signed written consent to act, which you must keep.
If the company will trade under a name other than its exact company name, it needs a separate business name registration.

steps.title: Each director gets a director ID
steps.detail: Every proposed director applies for their own director ID through ABRS before the company is registered. Online is fastest: sign in with myID (Standard or Strong), answer the identity questions and submit; your ID appears on screen. If you cannot get a myID with at least Standard strength, ABRS has other ways to apply depending on where you live.

steps.title: Choose and check the company name
steps.detail: Check the name on ASIC's name availability search. You can optionally reserve a name for up to 2 months using ASIC Form 410 if you are not ready to register.
steps.cost: Name reservation fee applies (amount not confirmed)

form.name: Form 410 Application for reservation of a name

steps.title: Prepare company details and consents
steps.detail: Prepare the registered office and principal place of business addresses, your rules (replaceable rules or constitution), share classes and numbers, member details and written consents, and each officeholder's details and signed consent to act.

steps.title: Register through the Business Registration Service
steps.detail: Apply to register the company (proprietary limited, public, or special purpose) in the Business Registration Service and pay the fee. You can add the company's ABN, GST, PAYG withholding and a business name in the same application. Some cases, such as hiding a residential address or an unlimited company, need a paper form or business service provider instead.
steps.timeframe: About 15 minutes; confirmation usually within 2 business days

steps.title: Receive your ACN, certificate and corporate key
steps.detail: The Business Registration Service emails the ACN and certificate of registration. ASIC posts the corporate key to the registered office; you need it to use ASIC's company officeholder portal. Show the company name wherever the company trades publicly, and put the name and ACN on required documents.

steps.title: Do the annual review every year
steps.detail: ASIC sends an annual statement after your review date (usually the registration anniversary). Check and update the company details, pass a solvency resolution, and pay the annual review fee. Keep company records and the share register up to date throughout the year.
steps.timeframe: Each year; late fees apply if not paid within 2 months of the review date

guides.title: Apply for an Australian Business Number (ABN)
guides.summary: An ABN is the 11-digit number that identifies your business to government and other businesses. It is free, and you need one to invoice properly, avoid having tax withheld from payments you receive, claim GST credits and get an .au domain name. You can only get one if you are carrying on, or starting, an enterprise.
guides.authority: Australian Business Register (ABR), administered by the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) as part of Australian Business Registry Services
guides.timeframe: Usually issued immediately at the end of the online application. If you get a reference number instead, the ABR aims to review it within 20 business days.
guides.cost_summary: Free. Applying for an ABN through the Australian Government costs nothing; private websites that charge a fee are not required.
before_you_start: Check you pass the entitlement test: you must be carrying on or starting an enterprise in Australia (or be a Corporations Act company). Signs of a business include significant commercial activity, an intention to make a profit shown by a business plan, repeated and systematic activity run in a business-like way, and relevant skill.

You are not entitled to an ABN for work you do as an employee (including apprentices, trade assistants and labourers, even if it is called contracting), or for a hobby. An employer should not make an ABN a condition of employment.

If you have not started trading yet, you should already have taken some start-up steps, such as advertising, setting up a website or social media, getting licences or insurance, leasing premises or equipment, giving quotes or applying for finance.

Choose your business structure first (sole trader, partnership, company or trust). It changes what the application asks and which other registrations you need, and changing structure later can mean a new ABN.
Have your tax file number (TFN) ready, plus the TFNs of any associates such as partners, directors or trustees. Being identifiable from your TFN speeds the application up.

Have ready: the date you need the ABN from (no more than six months in the future), your entity's legal name, business address, postal address, email and phone, your main business activity, the physical locations you operate from, and your ACN if you are a company.
Email addresses must be 5 to 200 characters with no spaces and must not begin with support@, sales@ or info@.
If you use a registered tax or BAS agent, have their agent number so they can be an authorised contact.

steps.title: Confirm you are entitled to an ABN
steps.detail: Read the ABR entitlement guidance and make sure your activity is an enterprise, not employment or a hobby. Keep evidence (business plan, quotes, licences, insurance, lease, adviser correspondence) because the ABR can review your entitlement at any time and ask you to prove you started, or took steps to start, your business from the date on your application. Applying without entitlement can lead to prosecution.

steps.title: Gather the information the application asks for
steps.detail: Collect your TFN and associates' TFNs, the ABN start date, legal name, business and postal addresses, contact details, main business activity, business locations, any previous ABN, your ACN (companies), and your tax or BAS agent number if you use one. You can save a part-finished application, but missing details will likely delay your ABN.

steps.title: Apply online through the Business Registration Service
steps.detail: Use the Australian Government Business Registration Service at register.business.gov.au. In the same application you can also apply for a business name, GST, an Australian company, PAYG withholding, fringe benefits tax, luxury car tax, fuel tax credits and wine equalisation tax, so you only enter your details once.
steps.timeframe: Most applications are finished in one sitting

steps.title: Read the outcome at the end of the form
steps.detail: If approved you get your 11-digit ABN on screen straight away; save or print the confirmation. If you get a reference number, the ABR needs to check your details and aims to review within 20 business days; check ABN Lookup and expect a confirmation letter within 14 days of approval. If refused, you get a refusal number and a letter within 14 days explaining why and your review rights.
steps.timeframe: Immediate, or up to 20 business days if reviewed

steps.title: Keep your ABN details up to date
steps.detail: Update your ABN details within 28 days of becoming aware of a change. Cancel your ABN if you close or sell the business, stop operating in Australia, or change structure (for example sole trader to company, sole trader to partnership, or partnership to company), and apply for a new one for the new structure.

Changing structure (for example sole trader to company) usually means cancelling the old ABN and getting a new one, and you may also need to update your business name with ASIC.
Some private websites charge to lodge an ABN application. The government application is free.

guides.title: Register a business name with ASIC
guides.summary: If you trade under any name other than your own personal name (or your company's exact name), you must register it as a business name with ASIC. Registration is national, so one registration covers every state and territory, and you choose 1 or 3 years.
guides.authority: Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC)
guides.timeframe: About 10 to 15 minutes online. Confirmation usually arrives within 2 business days if you pay by credit card, or 5 business days if you pay by BPAY, EFT or bank transfer.
guides.cost_summary: A$47 for 1 year or A$108 for 3 years (fees from 1 July 2026).
before_you_start: You must register a business name if you run a business in Australia and are not trading under your own name. You do not need one if you are a sole trader trading under only your first name and surname, a partnership trading under all partners' names, or a company trading under its exact company name.
You need an ABN, or an ABN reference number if your ABN application is still being processed. You can apply for both together in the Business Registration Service.
Check the name is free on ASIC's business names register: green means available, amber means ASIC will assess it after you apply, red means it is not available.
Also check IP Australia's TM Checker. You cannot register a name that someone already holds as a business name or trade mark, and a registered business name does not give you exclusive rights to it.

Have an address for service of documents (an Australian street address or PO Box) and a principal place of business (an Australian street address). Email and mobile are optional but email is where ASIC sends official notices and renewal reminders.
For a joint venture, have each participant's ABN.

steps.title: Check name availability
steps.detail: Search ASIC's business names register (green, amber or red result) and IP Australia's TM Checker. If the name is close to an existing trade mark, choose another name or get advice, because the business name register does not protect you against a trade mark owner.

steps.title: Get your ABN or ABN reference number
steps.detail: The business name must be held by an entity with an ABN. If you do not have one yet, apply for the ABN and the business name together in the Business Registration Service.

steps.title: Apply and pay online
steps.detail: Apply through the Business Registration Service or ASIC's online business name registration. Choose a 1-year or 3-year period, enter your service and principal place of business addresses, and pay. Registration takes effect once the application is submitted and payment clears (up to 24 hours), and ASIC then emails your record of registration.
steps.timeframe: Usually within 2 business days (card) or 5 business days (BPAY, EFT, bank transfer)

steps.title: Keep your details current
steps.detail: Tell ASIC about changes to your registration details, usually within 28 days. If your business structure changes and you get a new ABN, the business name must be moved to the new holder.
steps.timeframe: Usually within 28 days of a change

steps.title: Renew before it lapses
steps.detail: ASIC emails a renewal notice at least 30 days before your renewal date. Renew online through ASIC Connect or 'Pay now'. If you hold several business names or a company, you can ask ASIC to align renewal dates. If you do not renew on time, ASIC may cancel the name and someone else could register it.
steps.timeframe: Notice arrives at least 30 days before renewal

guides.title: Register for GST
guides.summary: Goods and services tax (GST) is a 10% tax you add to most sales once registered. You must register within 21 days once your GST turnover reaches A$75,000 (A$150,000 for non-profits), or from day one if you provide taxi, limousine or ride-sourcing travel. Registration is free.
guides.authority: Australian Taxation Office (ATO)
guides.timeframe: Register within 21 days of becoming required to. Check your turnover every month.
guides.cost_summary: The ATO lists no fee to register for GST.
before_you_start: You need an ABN first, or apply for GST at the same time as your ABN in the Business Registration Service.

You must register if your current or projected GST turnover is A$75,000 or more (A$150,000 or more for non-profit organisations). If you are new and expect to reach the threshold in your first year, register now.
You must register regardless of turnover if you provide taxi or limousine travel for passengers, including ride-sourcing, and whether you own, lease or rent the vehicle.
You also need GST registration if you want to claim fuel tax credits.
The ATO says people earning through the sharing economy or digital platforms may also need to register; check the ATO's sharing economy guidance for your activity.

GST turnover is your total business income (not profit), minus GST in your sales, certain sales to associates, input-taxed sales, sales not connected with an enterprise, and sales not connected with Australia. Current turnover is this month plus the previous 11; projected turnover is this month plus the next 11.
If you register voluntarily, you generally must stay registered for at least 12 months.

steps.title: Work out your GST turnover
steps.detail: Calculate current GST turnover (this month and the previous 11 months) and projected GST turnover (this month and the next 11). Leave out sales of business assets and sales made only because you are closing or substantially reducing the business. Repeat this check monthly.

steps.title: Register
steps.detail: Register through the Business Registration Service (with or after your ABN), ATO Online services for business, your registered tax or BAS agent, or by phoning the ATO business enquiries line. Choose the date your registration starts.
steps.timeframe: Within 21 days of reaching the threshold

steps.title: Set up your prices, invoices and records
steps.detail: Once registered, include GST in your prices for taxable sales, issue tax invoices, and keep records so you can claim GST credits on business purchases.

steps.title: Report and pay GST on your BAS
steps.detail: Most businesses under A$20 million GST turnover report quarterly on a business activity statement (BAS). You must report monthly if GST turnover is A$20 million or more. If you registered voluntarily with turnover under A$75,000 (A$150,000 non-profit), you can report annually. You can also elect to pay quarterly GST instalments and report actual GST once a year.

contacts.name: ATO business enquiries
contacts.hours: 8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday
contacts.note: Also used to request backdated GST registration. Have your ABN ready.

watch_out: If you should have registered but did not, you may have to pay the GST on past sales out of your own pocket, plus penalties and interest.
Taxi and ride-sourcing drivers must register before their first trip, even with very low income.
Backdating is possible but generally limited to 4 years (unless there is fraud or evasion). Ask by phoning the business enquiries line.
Voluntary registration generally locks you in for at least 12 months.
Claiming GST refunds when not entitled to an ABN or GST registration can lead to prosecution.

guides.title: Planning approval for a home based business or change of use (Cairns, CairnsPlan 2016)
guides.summary: Starting a business in your home, or moving a business into premises not approved for that use, is a material change of use under the Planning Act 2016. In Cairns some small home based businesses are accepted development and need no approval if they meet every requirement of CairnsPlan 2016 (version 3.1); otherwise you lodge a development application that is code or impact assessed.
guides.authority: Cairns Regional Council (Development and Planning), under the Planning Act 2016 and CairnsPlan 2016 version 3.1
guides.timeframe: Accepted development needs no application. Impact assessable applications include public notification for at least 15 business days. Overall decision timeframes were not published on the pages read.
guides.cost_summary: 2026-27 Cairns fees for a small scale (home based business) material change of use: A$1,135 code assessment or A$2,270 impact assessment. Pre-lodgement meetings are free. Infrastructure charges do not apply to home based businesses.
before_you_start: A home based business is a business run by the residents of a dwelling that is secondary to living there, small scale, and does not adversely affect neighbours. Working from home for an off-site employer is not a home based business.

Suitable examples: bed and breakfast, home office, small-scale beauty or massage, home-based childcare. Not suitable: shops, vehicle repair workshops, laundromats, swim schools, gyms, commercial-scale food preparation, cafes and food outlets.
No more than one non-resident employee.

Check the accepted development requirements in Part 5.5 (tables of assessment) and the Home based business code (9.2.15) of CairnsPlan 2016 version 3.1. If you meet all of them you need no development permit; if you do not, or Part 5.5 lists your use as code or impact assessable, you need a development application.
Signs: one home based business sign, maximum 0.3 square metres, not on or over Council land or road, needs no permit under Local Law No. 4.

Other approvals may still apply: building approval for extensions, a food business licence if you prepare food for sale, personal appearance services rules, and body corporate approval for units and townhouses.

steps.detail: Use Council's free pre-lodgement enquiry or meeting, or email townplanner@cairns.qld.gov.au, to confirm the zone, whether your business is accepted development, and what codes apply.

steps.title: Check the accepted development requirements
steps.detail: Compare your business against the Part 5.5 tables of assessment and the Home based business code compliance table. If you meet every requirement you can start (after any other approvals) without a development permit. Keep a record of how you comply.

steps.detail: If the business is code or impact assessable, prepare a development application addressing the relevant codes (a consultant town planner can help). Lodge online through Council's DA Online service, in person at 119-145 Spence Street, or by mail to Development and Planning, PO Box 359, Cairns QLD 4870.

steps.detail: Impact assessable applications must be publicly notified for at least 15 business days, usually with signs on site, letters to adjoining owners and a newspaper notice. Anyone can make a submission. Code assessable applications are not publicly notified.

steps.title: Receive the decision and follow the conditions
steps.detail: Council may approve with conditions limiting hours, employee numbers, vehicle trips or daily visitors. Keep within them.

guides.title: Building approval for a commercial fit-out (Cairns, Queensland)
guides.summary: Most building work, including many shop and cafe fit-outs, needs a building development approval (building permit) from a building certifier before work starts. In Cairns, Council does not do building certification, so you hire a QBCC-licensed private certifier. Plumbing, trade waste and fire safety approvals often run alongside it.
guides.authority: Private building certifier licensed by the Queensland Building and Construction Commission (QBCC), under the Building Act 1975 and Planning Act 2016; Cairns Regional Council for plumbing permits and trade waste; Queensland Fire Department for fire safety referrals
guides.timeframe: Set by your certifier; not published by Council or the State. Plumbing inspections are usually available the next business day if booked before 3pm. Trade waste approval can take up to 5 business days after you start trading.
guides.cost_summary: Certifier fees are set by the private certifier (not published). Cairns 2026-27 Council fees: plumbing permit A$520 for up to 6 fixtures plus A$37 per extra fixture; trade waste approval A$280 a year.
before_you_start: Get your lease, landlord consent and planning position clear first. A building approval does not replace a development approval if the planning scheme needs one for your use.

Ask a certifier early whether your fit-out needs approval. Only minor work listed as accepted (self-assessable) or exempt in Schedules 1 and 2 of the Building Regulation 2021 is free of building approval; internal commercial fit-outs are not specifically listed as exempt on Business Queensland's page.
Find a certifier on the QBCC's licensed certifier search. Council cannot recommend one.
Engage a designer or architect for plans and specifications. Engineers and other specialists may need to supply Form 15 compliance certificates for design.
If the building has fire services (sprinklers, alarms, hydrants), a fit-out that may affect them may need to be referred to the fire service unless it meets the scope reduction guidelines.
For food premises, line up a licensed plumber early: grease pre-treatment and new fixtures are permit work and need Council approval and inspection.

steps.title: Engage a private building certifier
steps.detail: Choose a QBCC-licensed building certifier and sign their engagement. The certifier lodges a notice of engagement (Form 56) with Council. They will tell you which plans, engineering and fire safety details they need.

steps.title: Prepare plans and design certificates
steps.detail: Have plans and specifications prepared for the fit-out. Where the certifier relies on another professional (for example a structural engineer or fire engineer), that person provides a Form 15 compliance certificate for building design or specification.

form.name: Form 15: Compliance certificate for building design or specification

steps.title: Fire safety referral if needed
steps.detail: If the work may affect installed special fire services, the certifier refers it to the Queensland fire service as an advice agency under the Planning Act 2016, unless the scope reduction guidelines apply. Partial fit-outs with a performance solution must be approved by the certifier and referred.
steps.cost: Fire service referral fees apply (see its fee advice)

steps.title: Get the building approval (decision notice)
steps.detail: The certifier assesses the application (Planning Act Form 2) against the National Construction Code and Queensland Development Code and issues a decision notice. Do not start building work until it is issued.

steps.title: Lodge a plumbing application for permit work
steps.detail: Only permit work needs a Council application. A licensed plumber does the work and either you or the plumber lodge through Council's Plumbing, Drainage and Wastewater forms page before work starts. Council inspects before work is covered up; the plumber books inspections (7:30am to 2:30pm weekdays). On completion Council issues a Form 19 final inspection certificate.
steps.timeframe: Inspections usually next business day if booked before 3pm; book 48 hours ahead
steps.cost: A$520 up to 6 fixtures, A$37 each extra fixture (2026-27)

steps.title: Apply for trade waste approval (food and other businesses)
steps.detail: If you discharge anything other than domestic sewage (food outlets, laundromats, workshops), contact Council's Trade Waste Team first. Your plumber installs any pre-treatment device (such as a grease arrestor) under a plumbing approval, then you lodge the online Trade Waste Approval application and a Trade Waste Officer does a final inspection.
steps.timeframe: Up to 5 business days after you start trading
steps.cost: A$280 a year application; renewals A$238 to A$340 a year (2026-27)

steps.title: Inspections during the work
steps.detail: The certifier (or a competent person) inspects the work at the stages set in the approval, as required by section 44 of the Building Regulation 2021. Competent persons may provide Form 16 inspection certificates for particular aspects.

steps.title: Final certificate before you open
steps.detail: At completion the certifier issues the final paperwork and lodges it with Council: a certificate of classification (Form 11) for commercial buildings, or a final inspection certificate (Form 21) where that applies. Your food licence final inspection usually follows once the fit-out is certified.

guides.title: QBCC contractor licence (builder or trade contractor)
guides.summary: In Queensland you need a QBCC contractor licence to do or supervise building work valued over A$3,300 (over A$1,100 for hydraulic services design), and for some work at any value, such as plumbing, drainage, gas fitting, fire protection, termite management and mechanical services. You must show technical qualifications, experience, a managerial qualification, and that your business meets the minimum financial requirements for its turnover.
guides.authority: Queensland Building and Construction Commission (QBCC)
guides.timeframe: Not stated for contractor licences generally; QBCC's plumbing and drainage page says processing usually takes a few weeks but to allow about 8 weeks.
guides.cost_summary: Fees depend on licence type (individual or company) and maximum revenue category. For example an individual SC2 licence (turnover up to A$800,000) was A$920.68 for a new applicant on QBCC's fee page last published 1 July 2025; fees rise each 1 July.
before_you_start: Choose the licence class that covers your work. QBCC has over 80 classes, including builder (low rise, medium rise, open, project management, and restricted classes such as kitchen bathroom and laundry, or shopfitting) and trade classes.
Choose individual or company licence. A company also needs a nominee supervisor who holds the relevant individual licence.

Technical qualifications: show you have the skills for the class (apprenticeship papers, RTO qualifications, recognition of prior learning). Experience requirements vary; builders typically show 2 or 4 years depending on qualifications, with referees licensed at the same or higher level.
Managerial qualification: for trade contractor and trade nominee supervisor licences, complete BSBESB402 Establish legal and risk management requirements of new business ventures.

Minimum financial requirements (MFR): current ratio at least 1:1, net tangible assets at least A$0 plus the minimum for your category, and a maximum revenue limit. SC1 (up to A$200,000) needs A$12,000 net tangible assets; SC2 (up to A$800,000) needs A$46,000; Category 1 (to A$3 million) needs A$46,001; Category 2 (to A$12 million) needs A$156,001.
Fit and proper: QBCC checks your history. You also need photo ID, right to work in Queensland, and evidence of your business structure (trading name, company, partnership or trust).

steps.title: Pick your class and licence type
steps.detail: Use QBCC's available licences list to confirm the class covers the work you will do, then decide on an individual or company licence and your maximum revenue category.

steps.title: Gather qualifications and experience evidence
steps.detail: Collect qualification certificates and an experience record for each project: dates, description and construction type, employer, supervisor and referee details. Referees must sign the reference declaration and may be contacted by a QBCC assessment officer.

steps.title: Complete the managerial qualification
steps.detail: Complete BSBESB402 with a registered training organisation (listed on training.gov.au) if your class requires it.

steps.title: Show you meet the minimum financial requirements
steps.detail: SC1 and SC2 applicants (turnover up to A$800,000) complete an MFR declaration on the application form. Category 1 to 7 applicants (over A$800,000) must lodge an MFR report prepared by an accountant. Some classes with professional indemnity insurance are exempt from financial reporting.

steps.title: Lodge the application and pay
steps.detail: Complete the contractor or nominee supervisor application form (or company form), attach documents and a passport photo, pay the fee, and lodge in person, by mail or email. Existing licensees can manage licences in the myQBCC portal.

steps.title: Keep meeting MFR and renew
steps.detail: Licences are renewed for 1 or 3 years. Category 1 to 7 licensees must lodge annual financial reporting; SC1 and SC2 sole traders do not lodge annual reports but must still meet MFR. Keep your turnover within your maximum revenue.

guides.title: QBCC plumbing and drainage licences (occupational and contractor)
guides.summary: In Queensland every person doing or supervising regulated plumbing or drainage work needs a QBCC occupational plumber and/or drainer licence, and anyone contracting for plumbing or drainage work (at any value) also needs a plumbing and drainage contractor licence. The occupational licence needs a Certificate III in Plumbing with a completed apprenticeship and 12 months' experience; the contractor licence adds a managerial qualification and minimum financial requirements.
guides.authority: Queensland Building and Construction Commission (QBCC)
guides.timeframe: Occupational licence applications are processed within 20 days (QBCC can take up to 20 more days if it needs information). Contractor licences usually take a few weeks; allow about 8 weeks.
guides.cost_summary: Occupational plumber licence: A$248.75 for 1 year including the A$80.90 annual administration fee (QBCC says fees increased 1 July 2026). Contractor licence fees follow the QBCC contractor fee table by revenue category.
before_you_start: Occupational plumber: Certificate III in Plumbing (QBCC lists CPC32413, including the drainage stream) with a completed apprenticeship and 12 months' plumbing experience.
Occupational drainer: CPC20712 Certificate II in Drainage or CPC32413, and 12 months' drainage experience. Combined plumber and drainer needs both.

If you lack the qualification or experience, or hold an interstate or overseas licence you cannot prove, you may get a 1-year provisional licence that cannot be renewed; you must work under a licensed occupational holder.
Work outside the occupational scope (for example some specialist work) needs an endorsement.

Contractor licence: you must also hold the occupational licence, complete BSBESB402 (older BSBSMB401 is in teach-out), meet MFR, and be fit and proper. Companies nominate an individual licensee to supervise.
Interstate (ACT, NSW, NT, SA, Tas, Vic, WA) or New Zealand licence holders can apply under mutual recognition while their home licence stays active.

guides.title: Electrical work licence and electrical contractor licence (Queensland)
guides.summary: In Queensland a person doing electrical work needs an electrical work licence (such as electrical mechanic), and any business doing electrical work for others needs an electrical contractor licence. The contractor licence needs a qualified technical person, a qualified business person, A$5 million public and products liability insurance and A$50,000 consumer protection cover, and is renewed every year.
guides.authority: Electrical Safety Office, Office of Industrial Relations (WorkSafe Queensland), under the Electrical Safety Act 2002 and Electrical Safety Regulation 2026
guides.timeframe: Processing times are not published. Work licences run for 5 years; contractor licences for 1 year.
guides.cost_summary: From 1 July 2026: electrical contractor licence application A$464.30 (renewal the same); electrical work licence application A$97.15. Part of each fee is refundable if the application does not proceed.
before_you_start: Electrical work licence (electrical mechanic): UEE30820 Certificate III in Electrotechnology Electrician, completed no more than 3 years before you apply; Queensland apprentices' RTOs submit a completion statement.

Each year you must have done CPR (and PTR for linespersons) within the last 12 months; at renewal you need skills maintenance within the last 2 years. Keep the certificates; they are not submitted but must be produced on request.

Contractor licence: nominate at least one qualified technical person (QTP) and one qualified business person (QBP); one person can be both. They must be the sole trader or an employee, a partner or employee, or a company director, officer, member or employee.

QTP: hold a current Queensland electrical work licence for at least 2 years (or equivalent evidence), and complete UEEEL0002 (within 3 years), UEEEL0030 and UEEEL0029. Less experience may get a contractor licence with reduced scope.
QBP: complete UEECD0007 and UEEEL0040, plus one of BSBESB402, a diploma-level or higher business qualification, or evidence of running a business for 5 years with a referee.

Insurance in the business's legal name: public and products liability of at least A$5,000,000 and consumer protection of at least A$50,000, also covering testing and certifying, faulty design and advice, and goods in your care. Confirm with your insurer it meets section 165 of the regulation.
You need a Digital ID to apply online, or call 1300 632 993 for an alternative.

steps.detail: Take out public and products liability insurance (minimum A$5 million) and consumer protection cover (minimum A$50,000) in the legal name of the applying business. You declare it when you apply; you do not upload the policy, but must produce it or insurer confirmation if audited.

steps.detail: Apply in the Electrical Licensing Portal. Nominate an authorised person (sole trader, partner, or director or executive officer), at least one QTP and one QBP. Pay by Visa or Mastercard through BPoint.

steps.detail: Each nominated QTP, QBP and authorised person gets an email to verify their identity and accept the nomination. The application does not proceed until at least one QTP and one QBP confirm.

steps.title: Renew every year
steps.detail: Contractor licences are issued for 1 year and must keep meeting eligibility (nominees and insurance) for the whole term. Renew on or before expiry; an expired licence can be reinstated within 12 months.

guides.title: Register as a health practitioner with Ahpra and your National Board
guides.summary: If you work in one of the 16 regulated health professions (for example medicine, nursing, physiotherapy, psychology, pharmacy or dentistry), you must be registered with your National Board through Ahpra before you practise. Ahpra registers individual practitioners; your business does not get its own Ahpra registration, but anyone advertising a regulated health service, including a business, must follow the advertising law.
guides.authority: Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (Ahpra) and the relevant National Board
guides.timeframe: Graduates: within about two weeks after the education provider confirms results. Internationally qualified: about 4 to 6 weeks. Previously registered: about 6 to 8 weeks.
guides.cost_summary: You pay an application fee plus a registration fee, set by your profession's Board. For example, general registration costs A$1,661 + A$1,102 for doctors (from 1 August 2026) and A$332 + A$193 for nurses and midwives (from 18 September 2025).
before_you_start: Check your profession is one of the 16 regulated ones: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health practice, Chinese medicine, chiropractic, dental, medical, medical radiation practice, midwifery, nursing, occupational therapy, optometry, osteopathy, paramedicine, pharmacy, physiotherapy, podiatry and psychology.
Have your identity documents ready for an online proof of identity check. International applicants need certified copies of their qualifications.

Ahpra runs an Australian criminal history check on every applicant (included in the fee). Overseas applicants may also need an international check, and you cannot be registered until the results are in.
Have evidence for your English language declaration (test results or another accepted pathway under your Board's standard).
Find your Board's fee schedule on its website under Registration; fees may differ if your principal place of practice is in NSW.
A clinic or practice business does not register with Ahpra, but each practitioner in it must be registered, and the business must follow the advertising rules for regulated health services.

steps.title: Create an Ahpra practitioner portal account
steps.detail: All registration applications are online. Create or log in to your Ahpra practitioner portal and start the application for your profession and registration type (for example general registration).

steps.title: Prove your identity and upload documents
steps.detail: Upload your identity documents and complete the online proof of identity check. Upload qualifications (certified copies if internationally qualified) and English language evidence. If documents are missing, you get 30 days to provide them.
steps.timeframe: 30 days to fix an incomplete application

steps.title: Pay the application and registration fees
steps.detail: Both the application fee and the registration fee are paid when you apply. The amounts are on your National Board's fee page. If you are granted registration in the last two months of the registration period, you do not pay the registration fee until the next renewal.

steps.title: Wait for checks and the Board's decision
steps.detail: Ahpra completes the criminal history check and assesses your application against the Board's registration standards. Check the public register to confirm your registration before you start practising.

steps.title: Get a Medicare provider number if you will bill Medicare
steps.detail: Once registered, apply to Services Australia for a Medicare provider number (and PBS prescriber number if relevant). Some professions can apply online through PRODA: My Details, then My Digital Provider Number Registration, then Apply; most get a number immediately. Others use a paper form (HW019 for medical practitioners). Apply early, as paper applications surge between December and April.

guides.title: Provider approval and service approval for an early childhood education and care service (Queensland)
guides.summary: To run a long day care, kindergarten, outside school hours care or family day care service under the National Quality Framework you need a provider approval (for you or your organisation) and a service approval (for each service). In Queensland you apply online through the National Quality Agenda IT System to the Department of Education's regulatory authority. Provider approval takes up to 60 days and service approval up to 90 days.
guides.authority: Queensland Department of Education, Early Childhood Regulatory Authority, under the Education and Care Services National Law
guides.timeframe: Provider approval: decision within 60 days of a complete application (can be extended by up to 30 days with your agreement). Service approval: within 90 days. Time spent waiting for your information does not count. October to January is a peak period.
guides.cost_summary: Qld fees published for 2026-27: provider approval A$364; centre-based service approval A$729 (small) to A$1,829 (extra-large); family day care service approval A$1,096; annual service fee A$329 to A$828.
before_you_start: Before applying, the department recommends completing ACECQA's National Law and Child Care Subsidy Approval eLearning course.

Fit and proper: individual applicants, and for organisations the applicant and every person with management or control of the service, are assessed. Regulators may request more information, an online knowledge assessment or an interview.
Individuals apply in the state where they live; companies, associations and partnerships apply where their principal office is. A trust cannot hold provider approval, but a trustee can.

For centre-based services, have premises information ready: plans by a building practitioner, planning and occupancy permits, building or classification certificates, soil assessment, and a water safety policy if there is a pool or water hazard. Some items (such as the occupancy certificate) can follow after construction but all are needed before approval.
Nominate at least one nominated supervisor and get their written consent.
Have the regulation 168 policies and procedures prepared (they are not lodged up front for centre-based services). Family day care must also lodge regulation 169 policies with the application.
Make sure planning approval for a childcare centre is in place or under way with Cairns Regional Council; service approval cannot be finalised without it.

steps.title: Apply for provider approval in the NQA IT System
steps.detail: Lodge the provider approval application online through the National Quality Agenda IT System with the fee. Include fitness and propriety information for the applicant and each person with management or control. Officers who will not have management or control can say so in writing.
steps.timeframe: Decision within 60 days of a complete application

steps.title: Apply for service approval at the same time
steps.detail: Lodge the service approval application online for each service, with the prescribed information for the service type (regulation 24, 25 or 26), the nominated supervisor's consent and the fee. Service approval cannot be granted until provider approval is granted. Applications are only accepted online.

steps.title: Receive the decision and display it
steps.detail: Approvals may be granted with or without conditions, or refused. Display the approvals at the premises. If refused, you can ask for internal review within 14 days using form AR01.

steps.detail: Once approved, pay the annual service fee on or before 1 July each year. Fees are indexed each year.

before_you_start: Check the service is higher risk: skin penetration where blood or body fluid release is expected, such as tattooing (including cosmetic tattooing and semi-permanent make-up), body piercing other than closed ear or nose piercing, implanting substances into the skin (hair, beads, cosmetic injectables), scarring or cutting, and tattoo removal.

Every operator and employee who provides higher risk services must hold HLTINF005 Maintain infection prevention for skin penetration treatments (older equivalents HLTIN402B, HLTIN402C and HLTIN2A are accepted). guides.title: Food business licence (Cairns Regional Council)
guides.summary: Most Queensland businesses that make food or sell unpackaged food, such as cafes, restaurants, takeaways, bakeries and food trucks, need a food business licence from their local council under the Food Act 2006. In Cairns you first get the premises design (fit-out) approved, then apply for the licence at least 30 days before trading and pass a final inspection before you open.
guides.authority: Cairns Regional Council (Licensing and Approvals / Environmental Health), under the Food Act 2006 (Qld)
guides.timeframe: Allow up to 30 days for the suitability of premises (fit-out) assessment, then apply for the licence at least 30 days before you plan to trade. The final inspection happens after fit-out; a licence copy is mailed within 2 days of a successful inspection.
guides.cost_summary: 2026-27 Cairns fees: A$450 suitability of premises (fit-out) assessment plus A$805 licence application for a medium or high risk premises (most cafes and restaurants) or A$450 for a low risk premises. Annual renewal is A$805 or A$450.
before_you_start: Check you actually need a licence. You generally do if you manufacture food or sell unpackaged food (cafes, restaurants, bars, takeaways). You do not if you only sell things like whole fruit and vegetables, drinks such as tea, coffee or soft drinks, ice, uncreamed cakes and biscuits, confectionery, chips or nuts. Exempt businesses must still follow food safety law.
The applicant must be a legal entity (a person or a company), not a business name and not your building contractor.

Get planning and building sorted first. Council checks that you hold any planning, development and footpath dining approvals the business needs, and whether the design and fit-out suit your type of food business.

Have a scaled floor plan and fit-out details ready (benches, sinks, hand basins, finishes, storage, cool rooms). Read Council's Fixed Food Business Operation and Construction Guideline before you design or sign a fit-out quote.

Work out your Standard 3.2.2A category. If you make and serve ready-to-eat potentially hazardous food you are category one and need a certified food safety supervisor, trained food handlers and records. If you only sell such food made elsewhere you are category two.

Check whether you need an accredited food safety program. You do if you cater off-site, if on-site catering is your main activity (or you cater for 200 or more people on 12 or more occasions in 12 months), if you are part of a private hospital, or if you serve potentially hazardous food to 6 or more vulnerable people (for example child care or nursing homes).
If you are buying an existing food business, a licence does not transfer automatically. Ask for a pre-sale inspection and apply for your own licence before settlement.
Most commercial kitchens also need a Trade Waste Approval from Council (grease pre-treatment) and plumbing permits for new fixtures. Plan these into the fit-out.

steps.title: Talk to Council before you commit to a lease or design
steps.detail: Call Council's Licensing and Approvals team on 1300 69 22 47 to confirm the premises can be used for food, what category your business will be, and whether you also need planning approval, trade waste approval or a footpath dining permit. Ask your landlord for any past food licence history of the site.

steps.title: Lodge the suitability of premises (fit-out) application
steps.detail: Submit the Suitability of Premises application with scaled plans and fit-out details. An Environmental Health Officer assesses it against the Food Act 2006 and Council's construction guideline. If it is approved you get a conditional approval letter. Do not start the fit-out until you have this letter and any building approval.
steps.timeframe: Generally up to 30 days, longer if information is missing

steps.title: Do the fit-out to the approved plans
steps.detail: Once you have the conditional approval letter and any other permits (such as a building approval from a private certifier and plumbing permits), fit out the premises exactly as approved. Changes from the approved plans can fail the final inspection.

steps.title: Apply for the food business licence
steps.detail: Lodge the Food Business Licence application at least 30 days before you want to trade. If you need a food safety program, submit the accredited program with the application. Council will not assess the licence until your design plans are approved; if you want to lodge both at once, call the Licensing and Approvals team first. Council may ask for more information, which extends the timeframe.
steps.timeframe: Lodge at least 30 days before trading
steps.cost: A$805 medium or high risk premises, A$450 low risk premises (2026-27)

steps.title: Book and pass the final inspection
steps.detail: When the fit-out is finished, request a final inspection. The officer checks the fit-out matches your approval letter. Use Council's final inspection checklist beforehand. If only minor items are outstanding you may get a provisional licence for up to 3 months with conditions; if those are not met the application is refused.
steps.timeframe: Licence copy mailed within 2 days of inspection
steps.cost: Included; reinspections are A$260 in business hours (2026-27)

guides.title: Food safety supervisor, food handler training and records (Standard 3.2.2A)
guides.summary: Every licensed food business in Queensland must have a food safety supervisor and tell Council who it is. Since 8 December 2023, cafes, restaurants, caterers and similar businesses that handle unpackaged ready-to-eat potentially hazardous food must also use a certified supervisor (certificate under 5 years old), make sure every food handler is trained, and (for category one) keep records that prove key food safety controls.
guides.authority: Cairns Regional Council (enforces in Cairns) under the Food Act 2006 (Qld) and Food Standards Code Standard 3.2.2A (Food Standards Australia New Zealand)
guides.timeframe: Appoint a certified supervisor before handling high-risk food; notify Council within 30 days of the licence being issued and within 14 days of any change.
guides.cost_summary: No Council fee to notify. The supervisor course is paid to a registered training organisation (price varies). Council's I'M ALERT food handler course is free.
before_you_start: Work out your category. Category one: caterers and food service businesses that make unpackaged potentially hazardous food into ready-to-eat food served without further processing (most cafes and restaurants). Category two: retailers of ready-to-eat potentially hazardous food that was handled unpackaged but not made on site (slicing, weighing, repacking, reheating and hot-holding do not count as making).

Category one needs all three tools: a certified food safety supervisor, trained food handlers, and substantiation (records) of critical controls. Category two needs a certified supervisor and trained food handlers.

Pick a supervisor who regularly handles food as part of their normal job and is reasonably available, meaning on site or easily contactable by phone while the business operates. Appointing someone who is never on site is not acceptable.

The supervisor certificate must come from a registered training organisation (or an organisation recognised by the food regulator) and be less than 5 years old. Check the course units on training.gov.au.
Every licensed food business in Queensland, not only category one and two, must have a food safety supervisor with relevant skills and authority to instruct staff.

steps.title: Choose and train your food safety supervisor
steps.detail: Enrol your nominated supervisor in a food safety supervisor course with a registered training organisation. Keep a copy of the certificate on site; the supervisor must be able to show it to an authorised officer on request. Larger businesses with several sites need a supervisor reasonably available for each site, not necessarily one per store.
steps.timeframe: Before you handle high-risk unpackaged food

steps.title: Train every food handler
steps.detail: Before staff handle unpackaged potentially hazardous food, make sure they have completed a food safety training course or have equivalent skills and knowledge in safe food handling, food contamination, cleaning and sanitising, and personal hygiene. Cairns Regional Council subscribes to the free I'M ALERT online course, which gives a training acknowledgement form and certificate. Keep evidence of each person's training.

steps.title: Set up records for critical controls (category one)
steps.detail: Keep records, or another method you can demonstrate to an officer, showing you control receiving, storing, processing, displaying and transporting potentially hazardous food, plus cleaning and sanitising. Typical records are delivery and fridge temperature logs, cooking and cooling checks, and cleaning schedules. FSANZ publishes record templates in Safe Food Australia Appendix 8.

form.name: FSANZ record templates (Safe Food Australia Appendix 8)

steps.title: Notify Cairns Regional Council of the supervisor
steps.detail: Give Council the supervisor's name and contact details within 30 days of your licence being issued. There is no fee. You can phone 1300 69 22 47, email regadmin@cairns.qld.gov.au or post to PO Box 359, Cairns QLD 4870.

steps.title: Keep Council updated
steps.detail: Notify Council within 14 days if a new person becomes supervisor, if the supervisor's contact details change, or if the supervisor stops being supervisor.

steps.title: Renew the supervisor certificate
steps.detail: The certificate must be less than 5 years old. Book a refresher course (if your provider offers one) or repeat the full course before it passes 5 years.

watch_out: Missing the 30-day notification after your licence is issued, or the 14-day notice after a change, is a breach; councils can issue fines for failing to notify.
A supervisor certificate older than 5 years does not count. Diarise the expiry date.
Naming an owner who is never on site, or does not handle food, as supervisor does not meet the 'reasonably available' test.
If your supervisor leaves, you must appoint and notify a replacement within 14 days. Train a second person as backup.
For category one, an officer can ask to see temperature and cleaning records; no records and no other way to show control is a breach.
Staff must be trained before they handle high-risk food, not after they start.

guides.title: Liquor licence (Queensland)
guides.summary: To sell or supply alcohol in Queensland you need a liquor licence or permit from the Office of Liquor and Gaming Regulation (OLGR). Cafes and restaurants usually need a commercial other (subsidiary on-premises) licence; small bars, hotels, nightclubs and bottle shops need other types. Most new applications take around 3 months and need advertising, a community impact statement unless waived, and trained staff.
guides.authority: Office of Liquor and Gaming Regulation (OLGR), Department of Justice (Queensland); Commissioner for Liquor and Gaming decides
guides.publisher: Office of Liquor and Gaming Regulation
guides.timeframe: Most new applications are finalised in around 3 months if everything is lodged and there are no issues; longer if you also apply for gaming machines or there are objections.
guides.cost_summary: An application fee (set each 1 July in OLGR's fee list) plus a criminal history check fee, then an annual licence fee due by 31 July. The 2026-27 base annual fee for a commercial other licence is 735.30 fee units, about A$833. Extra annual fee components apply for late trading hours and poor compliance history.
before_you_start: Pick the licence type. Commercial other (subsidiary on-premises): restaurants, cafes, function centres and similar where alcohol is secondary to the main business. Bar licence: small venues where drinking is the main business, seating up to 60. Commercial hotel: hotels and taverns, on and off-premises sales, needs a commercial kitchen and more than 60 seats. Nightclub: live entertainment is the main business. Subsidiary off-premises: takeaway alcohol secondary to the business.

Restaurants (not cafes) whose main activity is meals can ask for a takeaway wine condition: up to 1.5 litres (two bottles) sold only with a takeaway meal, 10am to 10pm. No other takeaway alcohol is allowed.
Check your development (planning) approval. It may restrict liquor or takeaway sales, and OLGR asks for town planning consent with the application.
You, and every person with a financial interest, must be fit and proper. Each individual party completes a personal details schedule and pays for a criminal history check.
Line up training: an individual licensee and every approved manager needs a current RMLV certificate (renew every 3 years); everyone who serves alcohol needs an RSA certificate.

Prepare a scale 1:100 layout plan of the licensed area, a location plan, a current title search, the registered survey plan and (for companies) a current company extract. Have your menu ready if you serve food.

steps.title: Confirm the licence type and conditions
steps.detail: Use Business Queensland's licence types page or the Business Launchpad to confirm which licence fits. Check the conditions that come with it, such as meal service requirements for restaurants, trading hours and the need for a licensee or approved manager on site.

steps.title: Prepare the application pack
steps.detail: Complete Form 1 (application for a liquor licence), Form 5 (personal details schedule) for each individual party, and Form 6 (registration of financial interest). Attach the 1:100 layout plan, location plan, town planning consent, title search, survey plan and company extract. Tick the options for a craft beer and artisan spirits promotional condition or takeaway wine with meals if you want them. Add an extended trading hours or catering endorsement (Form 18) request if needed.

form.name: Form 1: Application for a liquor licence

steps.title: Prepare a community impact statement (or ask for a waiver)
steps.detail: New licences (except community other) and some variations need a community impact statement covering your facilities, the local community area, positive and negative health and social impacts, harm mitigation, and evidence the area will not suffer from too many venues. Hotels, nightclubs, special facilities and trading after 2am also need consultation with residents and businesses within 200 m, a broader community survey and at least 8 key community advisers. Restaurants and cafes in a commercial complex that do not trade between midnight and 1am and have no amplified entertainment may ask the Commissioner in writing to waive it.

steps.title: Check whether you need a risk-assessed management plan
steps.detail: Some applications need a risk-assessed management plan (RAMP) describing how you will run the venue safely. Check OLGR's RAMP guidance for your licence type.

steps.title: Lodge and pay
steps.detail: Lodge the application with the prescribed application fee and criminal history check fee. OLGR's fee list is current from 1 July each year. The OLGR client portal is for existing licensees; new applicants follow the lodgement instructions on the application form.
steps.cost: Application fee per OLGR's current fee list

steps.title: Advertise the application
steps.detail: After lodging, OLGR may ask you to place a notice on each street frontage for 28 days, using the wording, size and timing OLGR sets. Your application also appears on OLGR's public register. Local government, police and members of the public can comment or object.

steps.title: Assessment and decision
steps.detail: OLGR assesses whether you are fit and proper, whether the premises are suitable, community impact, and any objections. If refused you can seek a review at the Queensland Civil and Administrative Tribunal (QCAT).

steps.title: Train staff before you trade
steps.detail: Make sure the individual licensee and approved managers hold RMLV (an RMLV holder is treated as RSA trained) and that every person who serves or supplies alcohol, including glass collectors and floor staff, holds RSA.

steps.title: Pay the annual fee each year
steps.detail: Annual fees are charged in advance each financial year and are due by 31 July. Your first fee is pro-rata to 30 June. Pay through the OLGR client portal. If you do not pay on time the licence is suspended, and cancelled if still unpaid 28 days after suspension.

steps.title: One-off events
steps.detail: Licensed hotels, nightclubs and subsidiary licensees catering at public events such as festivals need a commercial public event permit. Clubs and community groups selling to the public at one-off events such as fetes need a community liquor permit (check the exemption self-assessment first). Private functions away from your premises need a catering endorsement on your licence.

guides.title: Footpath dining permit (Cairns Regional Council)
guides.summary: To put tables, chairs, umbrellas, planter boxes or barriers on the Council footpath outside your cafe or restaurant in Cairns you need a footpath dining permit (a Commercial Use Activity permit under Council's local laws). You pay a one-off application fee for a 1, 2 or 3 year permit plus a rental fee per square metre that depends on the area of the city, and you must hold A$20 million public liability insurance.
guides.authority: Cairns Regional Council, under Local Law No. 11 (Local Government Controlled Areas and Roads) 2016 and Local Law No. 1 (Administration) 2016
guides.timeframe: Minimum 14 days and up to 30 days. Council will not accept an application with a start date less than 14 days after you submit it.
guides.cost_summary: 2026-27 application fee A$290 (1 year), A$525 (2 years) or A$750 (3 years), plus rental per square metre from A$11.90 (Area G) to A$247.20 (Area A).
before_you_start: Read Council's Best Practice Use of Footpaths Policy; applications are assessed against it, including pedestrian clearances and furniture standards.
If you do not own or hold a registered lease over the adjoining premises, get the landowner's written consent.
Get a certificate of currency for public liability insurance of at least A$20 million in the permit holder's name, noting Cairns Regional Council as an interested party.

guides.title: Workers' compensation accident insurance policy (WorkCover Queensland)
guides.summary: If your Queensland business employs workers, including casuals, apprentices and unpaid interns, you must insure them with a WorkCover Queensland accident insurance policy (unless you are a self-insurer). It takes 5 to 15 minutes to apply online. Being uninsured can cost you the unpaid premium plus a 100% penalty, and the cost of any claim plus 50%.
guides.authority: WorkCover Queensland (insurer); Workers' Compensation Regulatory Services, Office of Industrial Relations (regulator)
guides.timeframe: Apply online in about 5 to 15 minutes; you give your workers' start date when you apply. Renew every year between 1 July and 30 September.
guides.cost_summary: Premium = (estimated wages / 100) x your industry rate, plus GST and stamp duty. The 2026-27 average rate across Queensland is A$1.343 per A$100 of wages; your industry rate may be higher or lower. 3% discount for early payment.
before_you_start: You need a policy if you employ workers. A worker is generally a PAYG employee. Some contractors with ABNs are still workers in law; use WorkCover's worker determination tests or the ATO tools if you are unsure.
Apprentices are workers. Unpaid interns have been workers since 1 July 2020 (volunteers, school work experience and registered vocational placements are not).
Directors, partners, sole traders and trustees are not covered by the accident policy. Consider WorkCover's Workplace Personal Injury Insurance for yourself.

Have ready: your workers' start date, estimated wages from today to 30 June (before tax and super), a short description of your main business activity (sets your WorkCover Industry Classification), ABN and ACN, GST status, trading name and physical address, and trustee details if you pay through a trust.
Wages count before tax, superannuation and other deductions.

steps.title: Apply for an accident insurance policy
steps.detail: Apply online through WorkCover's new business system or by phone on 1300 927 928. Any authorised person, such as a director or finance officer, can apply. Give your expected start date, estimated wages, business activity and ABN.

steps.title: Pay the first premium

Pay online through WorkCover Connect, BPAY (biller code 182006), card (1300 132 278), direct debit or cheque. Interest-free payment plans are available for premiums over A$200.

steps.title: Renew and declare wages every year
steps.detail: Each July WorkCover contacts you. Declare actual wages for the year just ended and estimates for the new year, then pay between 1 July and 30 September. Declare by 31 August and pay in full by 16 September for a 3% discount; declaring by 31 August is also needed to set up a payment plan.

steps.title: Keep your policy accurate
steps.detail: Update WorkCover when your business activity, wages or structure changes. After 18 months your rate depends on your claims history (policy rating 80% to 120% of the industry rate), and businesses with wages over A$1.5 million move to experience-based rating.

guides.title: Register for PAYG withholding and set up as an employer
guides.summary: Before you pay your first employee you must register for pay as you go (PAYG) withholding with the ATO, even if no tax ends up being withheld. Taking on staff also brings other duties: Single Touch Payroll reporting, super paid with every pay (Payday Super from 1 July 2026, 12% of qualifying earnings), TFN declarations, Fair Work information statements and award pay rates.
guides.authority: Australian Taxation Office (ATO); Fair Work Ombudsman for pay and conditions
guides.timeframe: Register before your first payment that you need to withhold from. Super must reach the fund within 7 business days of each payday.
guides.cost_summary: The ATO lists no fee to register. Your ongoing costs are wages, 12% super, workers compensation insurance (state based) and STP-enabled payroll software.
before_you_start: Decide whether the worker is an employee or an independent contractor; the obligations are very different. Contractors who do not quote an ABN also trigger withholding.
Check the worker has the right to work in Australia. If you hire a working holiday maker, register as an employer of working holiday makers before you pay them.
Set up access to ATO Online services for business: get a Digital ID such as myID, then link it to your business in Relationship Authorisation Manager (RAM).
Get payroll software that is Single Touch Payroll (STP) enabled.

Find the award that covers the job (most small businesses are covered by one) and the minimum pay rate. The national minimum wage from the first full pay period on or after 1 July 2026 is A$26.44 an hour or A$1,005 a week for employees not covered by an award.
Choose a default super fund and a SuperStream-compliant way to pay. The Small Business Superannuation Clearing House closed permanently on 1 July 2026.
Arrange workers compensation insurance in your state or territory and work out whether payroll tax or fringe benefits tax applies to you.

Even if you do not have an ABN (for example you employ a nanny, cleaner, cook or gardener privately, or self-manage NDIS funds and employ staff), you still need to register for a PAYG withholding account.

steps.title: Register for PAYG withholding
steps.detail: With an ABN: register through the Business Registration Service, Online services for business, your registered tax or BAS agent, SBR-enabled software, or by phoning the ATO business line as an authorised contact. Without an ABN: phone the business line or lodge the Application to register a PAYG withholding account (NAT 3377). You must register before the first payment you need to withhold from, even if the amount withheld is nil.

form.name: Application to register a PAYG withholding account (NAT 3377)

steps.title: Give the employee their information statements
steps.detail: Give every new employee the Fair Work Information Statement before, or as soon as possible after, they start. Casual employees must also get the Casual Employment Information Statement, and employees on a fixed term contract must also get the Fixed Term Contract Information Statement. Make their award easily available to them.
steps.timeframe: Before or as soon as possible after the first day

steps.title: Collect the TFN declaration
steps.detail: Ask the employee to complete a Tax file number declaration (online through their ATO online services commencement forms, which they must complete within 28 days of starting, or on paper). If you use STP-enabled software you keep the form and do not send it to the ATO. If you are not using STP and get a paper form, complete section B and send it to the ATO within 14 days. If no TFN is provided and no exemption applies, withhold at the top rate plus Medicare levy (after 28 days if they have applied for a TFN).

steps.title: Offer choice of super fund
steps.detail: Give the employee a Superannuation standard choice form. If they do not choose a fund, you may need to ask the ATO for their stapled super fund before using your default fund. Give their TFN to the fund the next time you contribute or within 14 days of receiving it, whichever is later.

steps.title: Pay correctly and give a payslip
steps.detail: Pay at least the award or national minimum rate, withhold tax using the ATO tax tables, set the withheld tax aside, and give a payslip within one working day of payday. Use the Fair Work Pay Calculator to check rates, penalties and allowances.
steps.timeframe: Payslip within 1 working day of payday

steps.title: Report every pay through Single Touch Payroll
steps.detail: Report each employee's pay, tax withheld and super to the ATO through STP every time you pay them. Make an end-of-year finalisation declaration through STP by 14 July each year.

steps.title: Pay super with every pay (Payday Super)
steps.detail: From 1 July 2026 you must pay super guarantee of 12% of qualifying earnings (ordinary time earnings, paid leave, allowances, bonuses, commissions and superable salary sacrifice) so it is received by the employee's fund within 7 business days after each payday. For a new employee, or an employee who has moved to a new fund, the first contribution has 20 business days. Pay through a SuperStream-compliant method.
steps.timeframe: Received by the fund within 7 business days of payday

steps.title: Report and pay withheld tax on your BAS
steps.detail: Include PAYG withholding amounts on your business activity statement and pay the ATO the amounts you withheld.

steps.title: Keep records
steps.detail: Keep employment records for 7 years and tax and super records for 5 years, stored safely. When employment ends, give final pay (including unused annual leave) within 7 days.

The Small Business Superannuation Clearing House closed on 1 July 2026; do not rely on it.
Calling an employee a contractor, or asking them to get an ABN, does not change their legal status and can leave you owing tax, super and entitlements.
Underpaying award rates is a common and costly mistake. Check the award and the Pay Calculator before the first pay.

guides.title: Register with AICIS before you import or manufacture industrial chemicals
guides.summary: If you import or manufacture industrial chemicals for commercial purposes in Australia, including products that contain them such as cosmetics, cleaning products, paints and inks, your business must be registered with the Australian Industrial Chemicals Introduction Scheme (AICIS) before you introduce them. Registration runs for a registration year from 1 September to 31 August, and introducing chemicals while unregistered is an offence under the Industrial Chemicals Act 2019.
guides.authority: Australian Industrial Chemicals Introduction Scheme (AICIS)
guides.timeframe: Register online before your first introduction; the 2026-27 registration year runs 1 September 2026 to 31 August 2027, and you renew each year before 1 September. Annual declarations are due by 30 November after each registration year ends.
guides.cost_summary: For 2026-27 (from 1 September 2026) you pay an A$85 registration fee plus a levy based on the value of chemicals you introduced in the previous financial year. Because of a one-off 90% levy discount, totals range from A$85 (level 1, under A$50,000) to A$3,585 (level 8, A$15 million or more). No GST applies.
before_you_start: Work out whether you are an introducer: AICIS says anyone who imports or manufactures industrial chemicals for commercial purposes must register, including businesses, sole traders and individuals, and including people importing products that contain industrial chemicals.

Add up the value of the industrial chemicals you imported or manufactured in the previous financial year (for 2026-27 registration, 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026). This sets your registration level. If you are registering for the first time and introduced nothing in that period, you are level 1.
Have your business details ready so you can enrol in AICIS Business Services, the online portal used for registration, renewals and declarations.

Be ready to categorise every chemical you introduce. Each chemical (including each ingredient in a mixture) must fall into one of five categories: listed, exempted, reported, assessed, or commercial evaluation authorisation. AICIS publishes free decision tools to help.

Set up a record-keeping system from day one. AICIS says you must keep records for 5 years, even after you stop introducing the chemical, and provide them within 20 working days if asked (stated for assessed introductions).
If you will not introduce industrial chemicals after 31 August, tell AICIS through the 'advise of non-renewal' option in AICIS Business Services rather than just letting registration lapse.

steps.title: Work out your registration level
steps.detail: Use the AICIS registration calculator. Your level is based on the total value of industrial chemicals you imported or manufactured in the previous financial year (1 July to 30 June). The calculator also shows your fee and levy. Level 1 is A$0 to A$49,999 and level 8 is A$15,000,000 or more.

steps.title: Enrol in AICIS Business Services
steps.detail: New users create an account in AICIS Business Services, the AICIS online portal. Follow the AICIS guidance on creating an account. Renewing users simply log in. AICIS has tips on usernames and resetting passwords if you are locked out.

steps.title: Register or renew for the registration year
steps.detail: In AICIS Business Services, open the Registration section and select the registration year (2026-27). Enter your registration level and pay the registration fee and levy. You must be registered before you introduce industrial chemicals on or after 1 September 2026.
steps.timeframe: Before your first introduction in the registration year (registration year starts 1 September)
steps.cost: A$85 to A$3,585 for 2026-27 depending on level

steps.title: Categorise each chemical before you introduce it
steps.detail: For every chemical, decide its category. Listed: already on the Australian Inventory of Industrial Chemicals; meet any listing terms. Exempted: very low risk; no pre-notification, but some need a once-off post-introduction declaration. Reported: low risk; submit a once-off pre-introduction report before you start. Assessed: medium to high risk; you need an assessment certificate (fee applies) before you import or manufacture. Commercial evaluation authorisation: time-limited, for testing commercial viability (fee applies).
steps.timeframe: Before introduction (reported and assessed categories need action before you import)
steps.cost: No fee for listed, exempted or reported; fees apply for assessment certificates and commercial evaluation authorisations

steps.title: Keep records for every introduction
steps.detail: Keep records showing how you categorised each chemical and that you met the category requirements. AICIS says its decision tools are general guidance only and a completed decision tool is not enough on its own to meet your record-keeping obligations. Keep records for 5 years.

steps.title: Lodge your annual declaration
steps.detail: After each registration year, declare in AICIS Business Services that the chemicals you introduced were authorised. Submissions open in August. If you introduced nothing, select 'Did not introduce' in the portal. Example from AICIS: introductions between 1 September 2023 and 31 August 2024 had to be declared by 30 November 2024.
steps.timeframe: Due 30 November after the end of each registration year

steps.title: Renew every year, or tell AICIS you are stopping
steps.detail: Renew in AICIS Business Services for the new registration year before you introduce chemicals on or after 1 September. If you are stopping, use 'advise of non-renewal' for the new year.

Small importers of cosmetics, soaps, cleaning products, fragrances and similar goods often do not realise they are chemical introducers. Importing a product that contains an industrial chemical counts.

The 90% levy discount is one-off for 2026-27 only. From 2027-28 levies return to 2025-26 levels with two years of indexation, so a level 5 business that pays A$295 now could pay over A$2,180 next year.

Missing the 30 November annual declaration is a separate compliance failure, even if you are registered. If you imported nothing, you still select 'Did not introduce'.
